guarantees.claim: tl_err is driven by the output err_o of the tlul_err instance u_err.
The static assertion ensures that local parameter RegDw matches the top-level bus width TL_DW at compile time.

assumptions.claim: The inputs clk_i, rst_ni, and tl_i provided to u_err are stable and meet the timing/validity requirements of tlul_err.
assumptions.cond: every cycle where tl_err is observed
assumptions.risk: If clk_i has glitches, rst_ni is not properly deasserted, or tl_i does not follow TL-UL protocol, u_err may produce incorrect err_o, leading to false or missed bus-error detection.

uncertain_points.claim: The error-detection behavior of tlul_err (u_err) is opaque; the conditions under which err_o is asserted and whether all TL-UL protocol violations are correctly captured cannot be verified from this module alone.
uncertain_points.risk: A bug in tlul_err may fail to assert err_o on a protocol violation, allowing an illegal access to proceed silently, or may spuriously assert err_o, triggering unnecessary fault handling and potentially masking real security alerts.

formal_sketch.consequent: The error-detection behavior of tlul_err (u_err) is opaque; the conditions under which err_o is asserted and whether all TL-UL protocol violations are correctly captured cannot be verified from this module alone

security_implications: The tl_err signal indicates a TL-UL bus error. If the u_err logic (not visible here) is defective, a protocol-level violation (e.g., illegal address, access outside allowed region) may go undetected, allowing unauthorized reads/writes to security-critical registers or memories. Conversely, a false tl_err could lead to spurious alert escalation that degrades availability. The static width assertion prevents mismatched bus width which could otherwise cause silent data truncation or extractions.
